question: Ticket 1d23d635f7ca repairs the red seal on cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_hollow.py, but the harbor will not cross BUILDME onto a red-sealed proof and the ticket has no other proof. Should the harbor let BUILDME clear onto a red proof when the crossing's own ticket is the one that repairs it (the PROVED rung still demanding a green seal), or should a repair like this go some other way?
why_it_blocks: clearance.py's proven-space rung (rule 2) refuses BUILDME onto any named proof whose seal is red, and test_hollow.py is red only because of the decayed subject this ticket repairs; naming a different green proof instead poisons the PROVED union (it declares no tooth for 1d23), so the boat has no legal BUILDME crossing
answer: measured: settled by 56280fc01410 PROVED 2026-10-31 (commit df6b583a, outline 19.14.8.1): at BUILDME the proven-space rule follows the ticket's kind — a code-seam names its own not-yet-proven proof (x), a bug names the red it fixes (y). 1d23d635f7ca is a code-seam, so test_hollow.py's PROVES names it and BUILDME clears onto it; PROVED still demands a green seal.
